subject.title: Memory MVP: define SQLite schema and canonical record model

question: Should v1 durable memory move to typed SQLite records in memory-core, stay Markdown-native with tool-managed blocks, or use a staged hybrid with one clearly named source of truth?
rationale: Current main already uses SQLite for indexing and plugin state while public docs still make Markdown the durable memory source; the issue would define a new persistent record contract and migration boundary that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design typed SQLite records
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical schema design and require a maintainer-approved record model, migration plan, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Stay Markdown-native
options.body: Treat durable memory blocks in Markdown as the product source of truth and close or rewrite this issue around indexing and CRUD improvements only.

options.title: Stage a hybrid
options.body: Define a narrow bridge where SQLite stores typed metadata only after maintainers specify which layer owns edits, status, and provenance.

recommendation.title: Design typed SQLite records
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical schema design and require a maintainer-approved record model, migration plan, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history across memory-core, memory SDK, and storage-boundary changes involved in this decision.
